rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eating follows the preceding scene: Satan's prompting led Adam to eat, and Eve ate with him.
rows.anchor: أي فعمل آدم بوسوسة الشيطان فأكل من الشجرة وأكلت حواء معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan addressed his temptation to Adam, intending both to eat, because a wife naturally follows her husband.
rows.anchor: بأن اقتداء المرأة بزوجها مركوز في الجبلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is coordinated with eating: both ate, while Adam deliberately violated God's prohibition against that tree.
rows.anchor: وعصى آدم ربه } عطف على { فأكلا منها }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam was Eve's example, so she followed him; the author connects this duty of care to 66:6.
rows.anchor: في هذا المعنى قال الله تعالى : { يا أيها الذين آمنوا قوا أنفسكم وأهليكم نارا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghawā is the opposite of sound guidance and denotes corrupt conduct or false belief.
rows.anchor: فهي عمل فاسد أو اعتقاد باطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam was not yet a prophet and was in a realm without legal accountability; his act breached divine discipline.
rows.anchor: دليل على أنه لم يكن يومئذ نبيئا ، ولأنه كان في عالم غير عالم التكليف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This episode establishes neither that prophets may sin nor that they may not, since Adam was outside a world of legal responsibility.
rows.anchor: وليس في هذه الآية مستند لتجويز المعصية على الأنبياء ولا لمنعها

words: ثم اجتباه ربه فتاب عليه وهدى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parenthesis reports Adam's restoration after the expulsion, as in al-Baqara, and quickly shows his eventual rectification.
rows.anchor: لأن الاجتباء والتوبة عليه كانا بعد أن عوقب آدم وزوجه بالخروج من الجنة كما في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ijtibāʾ means selection; Ibn ʿĀshūr points to its use alongside guidance in 6:87 and 16:121.
rows.anchor: والاجتباء : الاصطفاء . وتقدم عند قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance means directing to benefit; paired with selection in the Qur'an, it denotes prophethood.
rows.anchor: والهداية : الإرشاد إلى النفع . والمراد بها إذا ذكرت مع الاجتباء في القرآن النبوءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The descent announcement answers the question raised by Adam's disobedience and deviation: what consequence followed?
rows.anchor: لأن الإخبار عن آدم بالعصيان والغواية يثير في نفس السامع سؤالا عن جزاء ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker is Adam's Lord, and the command addresses Adam and Iblis.
rows.anchor: عائد إلى { ربه } ( طه : 121 ) من قوله { وعصى آدم ربه } والخطاب لآدم وإبليس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The descent is a creative command: they could not leave the garden for earth without God's act of creation.
rows.anchor: لأنهما عاجزان عن الهبوط إلى الأرض إلا بتكوين من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jamīʿan is a singular noun expressing all members of a plural set, invariant for gender and number, and accusative as a circumstantial qualifier.
rows.anchor: اسم لمعنى كل أفراد ما يوصف بجميع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The enmity clause is a second circumstantial qualifier of the descent command.
rows.anchor: وجملة بعضكم لبعض عدو } حال ثانية من ضمير { اهبطا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam and Iblis are commanded to descend; Eve follows her husband.
rows.anchor: فالمأمور بالهبوط من الجنة آدم وإبليس وأما حواء فتبع لزوجها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural address to Adam and Iblis includes their descendants, founders of humankind and the satanic kind.
rows.anchor: وخوطبا بضمير الجمع لأنه أريد عداوة نسليهما ، فإنهما أصلان لنوعين نوع الإنسان ونوع الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Descent introduces humanity to a mixed world of good and evil and realities and illusions, unlike the garden's pure world; this change was inherent in human nature.
rows.anchor: إنباء بأنهم يستقبلون في هذه الدنيا سيرة غير التي كانوا عليها في الجنة لأنهم أودعوا في عالم خليط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is to Adam as the ancestor of humankind and anticipates that descendants will follow him.
rows.anchor: لآدم باعتبار أنه أصل لنوع الإنسان إشعارا له بأنه سيكون منه جماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis is excluded from this guidance command because God disclosed his enduring evil; asking him to seek guidance would be pointless, unlike addressing Abū Jahl.
rows.anchor: ولا يشمل هذا الخطاب إبليس لأنه مفطور على الشر والضلال إذ قد أنبأه الله بذلك

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: A report transmitted by al-Dāraquṭnī says each person, including the Prophet, has a jinn companion; the Prophet's companion became Muslim through God's aid.
rows.anchor: رواه الدارقطني أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report does not mean the Prophet invited his companion to Islam; God inspired the companion to command good.
rows.anchor: فلا يقتضي أنه دعاه للإسلام ولكن الله ألهم قرينه إلى أن يأمره بالخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here guidance means directing someone to good.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالهدى : الإرشاد إلى الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God charges Adam and his descendants to follow God's messengers and divine revelation.
rows.anchor: وصاية الله آدم وذريته باتباع رسل الله والوحي الإلهي

rows.speaker: علماء الإسلام
rows.claim: Many Muslim scholars hold that knowledge of the one God is innate in human reason or widespread across generations.
rows.anchor: قال كثير من علماء الإسلام : إن معرفة الإله الواحد كائنة في العقول

rows.speaker: كثير من علماء الإسلام
rows.claim: Many Muslim scholars hold that polytheists in periods without messengers are not excused from punishment.
rows.anchor: لم يعذر أهل الشرك في مدد الفتر التي لم تجىء فيها رسل للأمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first two clauses have already been interpreted in their parallel passage in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم تفسير نظير الجملتين الأولين في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following guidance from God's messengers prevents every kind of worldly misguidance; the negative construction is universal.
rows.anchor: سلم من أن يعتريه شيء من ضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human-made religious systems cannot ensure freedom from error because of oversight, conflicting evidence, customs, and appeasing leaders or nations.
rows.anchor: بسبب غفلات ، أو تعارض أدلة ، أو انفعال بعادات مستقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Socrates illustrates the limits of human wisdom: he disguised moral instruction in animal tales and, despite not deifying the gods, ordered a rooster offered to Hermes.
rows.anchor: وهذا سقراط وهو سيد حكماء اليونان قد كان يتذرع لإلقاء الأمر بالمعروف في أثينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Messengers receive revelation from the all-knowing God, are supported and protected from appeasing whims, and are formed and steadfast for their mission.
rows.anchor: الرسل الذين يتلقون الوحي من علام الغيوب الذي لا يضل ولا ينسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised freedom from wretchedness concerns the afterlife: avoiding error in this life saves one from the misery described for those who turn away in 20:124.
rows.anchor: هو شقاء الآخرة لأنه إذا سلم من الضلال في الدنيا سلم من الشقاء في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍank is a verbal noun from ḍanuka and retains one form regardless of the gender of its described noun, hence its use with feminine maʿīsha.
rows.anchor: والضنك : مصدر ضنك ، من باب كرم ضناكة وضنكا

rows.speaker: عنترة
rows.claim: Ḍank means narrow and can figuratively describe hardship; ʿAntara's verse uses it of a difficult place to stay.
rows.anchor:
قال عنترة :
إن يلحقوا أكرر وإن يستلحموا
أشدد وإن نزلوا بضنك أنزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrow life is inner distress: a person anxiously accumulates possessions and neglects virtue, even when outward comfort makes life look good.
rows.anchor: وهو هنا بمعنى عسر الحال من اضطراب البال وتبلبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Resurrection blindness depicts worldly blindness to guidance and salvation; it marks God's anger and exclusion from mercy.
rows.anchor: تمثيلا لحالته الحسية يومئذ بحالته المعنوية في الدنيا ، وهي حالة عدم النظر في وسائل الهدى والنجاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Blindness in the first instance is figurative, while blindness at resurrection is real.
rows.anchor: فأعمى الأول مجاز وأعمى الثاني حقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question begins a new sentence, and God's reply is separated because it continues the dialogue.
rows.anchor: قال رب لم حشرتني أعمى } مستأنفة استئنافا ابتدائيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse indicates that humanity was warned from its beginning against misguidance and polytheism, with warning embedded in human nature.
rows.anchor: في هذه الآية دليل على أن الله أبلغ الإنسان من يوم نشأته التحذير من الضلال والشرك

rows.speaker: كثير من علماء الإسلام
rows.claim: Many Muslim scholars hold that polytheists among peoples living between revealed laws deserve punishment.
rows.anchor: قال كثير من علماء الإسلام : بأن الإشراك بالله من الأمم التي يكون في الفتر بين الشرائع مستحق صاحبه العقاب

rows.speaker: أهل السنة والمعتزلة
rows.claim: Ahl al-Sunna and all Muʿtazilites hold that reason makes knowledge of God obligatory.
rows.anchor: وقال جماعة من أهل السنة والمعتزلة قاطبة : إن معرفة الله واجبة بالعقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an invokes this warning to alert its hearers not to turn away from God's remembrance and to warn them of a like fate.
rows.anchor: المقصود من ذكرها في القرآن تنبيه المخاطبين بالقرآن إلى الحذر من الإعراض عن ذكر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'Likewise' points back to the questioned blindness: the condemned had forgotten God's signs and refused to consider them when urged, so their fate fits their conduct.
rows.anchor: مثل ذلك الحال التي تساءلت عن سببها كنت نسيت آياتنا حين أتتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage uses three instances of ellipsis: the gathering also leaves the person forgotten, and the reply implies prior blindness to the signs as well as present blindness.
rows.anchor: وقد ظهر من نظم الآية أن فيها ثلاثة احتباكات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgetting in both places is a metaphor or metonymy for being deprived of mercy's benefits.
rows.anchor: والنسيان في الموضعين مستعمل كناية أو استعارة في الحرمان من حظوظ الرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading makes this a continuation of God's rebuke to the person resurrected blind, with the conjunction linking it to the preceding sentence.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن تكون من حكاية ما يخاطب الله به من يحشر يوم القيامة أعمى قصد منها التوبيخ له والتنكيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is a closing lesson to listeners rather than part of the divine address, with the conjunction introducing a parenthetical conclusion to the story.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون تذييلا للقصة وليست من الخطاب المخاطب به من يحشر يوم القيامة أعمى

words: من أسرف ولم يؤمن بآيات ربه
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here excess means false belief, disbelief, and stubbornly denying the Lord's signs.
rows.anchor: الاعتقاد الضال وعدم الإيمان بالآيات ومكابرتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison points to the narrow worldly life described for those who turn away: God gives the same kind of recompense to those who reject revelation.
rows.anchor: والمشار إليه بقوله { وكذلك } هو مضمون قوله { فإن له معيشة ضنكا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As a story conclusion, the afterlife punishment is contrasted with the worldly hardship of 20:124.
rows.anchor: ليس من حكاية خطاب الله للذي حشره يوم القيامة أعمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God addresses the resurrected man: his afterlife punishment is worse and lasts longer than worldly punishment.
rows.anchor: فالمراد بعذاب الآخرة العذاب الذي وقع فيه المخاطب ، أي أشد من عذاب الدنيا وأبقى منه لأنه أطول مدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question follows the threat in 20:127, rebuking idolaters for ignoring earlier peoples who shared their rejection of God and revelation.
rows.anchor: تفريع على الوعيد المتقدم في قوله تعالى : { وكذلك نجزي من أسرف ولم يؤمن بآيات ربه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural pronouns target living Meccan polytheists indirectly warned by the context, as shown by their walking among the ruins.
rows.anchor: فضمائر جمع الغائبين عائدة إلى معروف من مقام التعريض بالتحذير والإنذار بقرينة قوله { يمشون في مساكنهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance is borrowed for intellectual clarification, treating reason as sense perception; the verb takes a lām, as in 7:100.
rows.anchor: مستعارة للإرشاد إلى الأمور العقلية بتنزيل العقلي منزلة الحسي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative كم suspends يهدي from taking an object, asking how many generations God destroyed.
rows.anchor: عن العمل في المفعول لوجود اسم الاستفهام بعدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subject may be an implicit reference to God.
rows.anchor: ضمير دل عليه السياق وهو ضمير الجلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the question itself is the subject, and the verb is treated as intransitive with its object omitted.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الفاعل مضمون جملة { كم أهلكنا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The walking clause is circumstantial, describing the pronoun governed by lām; their access to the ruins makes their failure to understand more astonishing.
rows.anchor: حال من الضمير المجرور باللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The destroyed peoples are ʿĀd and Thamūd; Arabs passed their dwellings on routes to Yemen, Najrān, and Syria.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالقرون : عاد وثمود . فقد كان العرب يمرون بمساكن عاد

words: إن في ذلك لآيات لأولي النهى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final clause explains the rebuke: their predecessors' destruction supplies signs, and emphatic particles mark the claim as important and causal.
rows.anchor: وجملة { إن في ذلك لآيات لأولي النهى } في موضع التعليل للإنكار والتعجيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ending closes the debate and echoes the opening: the Prophet has delivered guidance, so he may take comfort in completing his mission while the heedless remain astray until truth becomes clear.
rows.anchor: وهي قوله { ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتشقى إلا تذكرة لمن يخشى } ( طه : 2 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After earth's creation comes heaven by contrast: the earth passage states its benefits, while heaven's creation shows no evident human benefit.
rows.anchor: ناسب بحكم الطباق ذكر خلق السماء عقبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since heaven's benefit is not apparent, the passage highlights people's refusal to reflect on its signs of profound wisdom rather than explicitly thanking them.
rows.anchor: ذكر إعراضهم عن التدبر في آيات خلق السماء الدالة على الحكمة البالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky's preservation embeds a blessing: celestial bodies or their parts do not fall on earth, destroy people, or ruin the land and its usefulness.
rows.anchor: حفظ السماء من أن تقع بعض الأجرام الكائنة فيها أو بعض أجزائها على الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A saqf is a roof laid on house walls, not a tent covering; calling the sky a roof is a direct simile, as 13:2 says it has no earthly pillars.
rows.anchor: ولا يقال السقف على غطاء الخباء والخيمة . وأطلق السقف على السماء على طريقة التشبيه البليغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about turning away is circumstantial; heaven's signs include celestial bodies and motions as well as clouds, lightning, and thunder.
rows.anchor: في موضع الحال . وآيات السماء ما تشتمل عليه السماء من الشمس والقمر والكواكب والشهب

words: وهو الذي خلق الليل والنهار والشمس والقمر
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite nominal clause presents creation as a benefaction and restricts it, countering the polytheists' implied claim that idols share in creation and divinity.
rows.anchor: سيقت في معرض المنة بصوغها في صيغة الجملة الاسمية المعرفة الجزأين لإفادة القصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage uses 'created' because its lesson and blessing concern these entities themselves, not their being made in a particular state.
rows.anchor: لا في إيجادها على حالة خاصة ، جيء هنا بفعل الخلق لا بفعل الجعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night's creation is one instance of creating darkness; darkness is absence and precedes existence, while night is earth's shadow as sunlight turns away.
rows.anchor: فإن الظلمة عدم والنور وجودي وهو ضد الظلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Daylight results from the sun and its rays reaching the earth's illuminated hemisphere, so mentioning the sun after day points to daylight's origin.
rows.anchor: فهو بخلق الشمس ومن توجه أشعتها إلى النصف المقابل للأشعة من الكرة الأرضية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon is mentioned alongside the sun and as a benefaction that gives people some light during part of the darkness.
rows.anchor: وللتذكير بمنة إيجاد ما ينير على الناس بعض النور في بعض أوقات الظلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explanatory sentence answers how the celestial bodies move without colliding or appearing out of time: each travels in its own expanse.
rows.anchor: سؤالا عن كيفية سيرها وكيف لا يقع لها اصطدام أو يقع منها تخلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural masculine pronoun refers to the sky's signs and specifically the sun and moon; masculine nouns such as moon and planet support its form.
rows.anchor: وضمير { يسبحون } عائد إلى عموم آيات السماء وخصوص الشمس والقمر

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf explains that the rational plural continues the personification begun by describing celestial bodies as swimming.
rows.anchor: وقال في ( الكشاف ) : ( إنه روعي فيه وصفها بالسباحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fī falak is the predicate, kull is the subject, and its nunation replaces an annexed noun; kull is definite in sense and each object has its own orbit.
rows.anchor: ظرف مستقر خبر عن { كل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The swimming clause is circumstantial; swimming is a metaphor for unimpeded travel through spacious paths that do not intersect.
rows.anchor: وجملة { يسبحون } في موضع الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lexicographers and commentators define falak as a celestial orbit, though Ibn ʿĀshūr notes they do not attest this use in pre-Islamic Arabic.
rows.anchor: والفلك فسره أهل اللغة بأنه مدار النجوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr suspects falak was a Qur'anic term adopted by Muslim scholars, transferred from the circular sea-wave and ultimately the spindle whorl.
rows.anchor: والأظهر أن القرآن نقله من فلك البحر وهو الموج المستدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven-letter phrase reads identically backward and forward, forming a smooth and useful palindrome; 74:3 gives a similar example without the conjunction.
rows.anchor: ومن بدائع الإعجاز في هذه الآية أن قوله تعالى : { كل في فلك } فيه محسن بديعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Sakkākī calls this pattern al-maqlūb al-mustawī, a variety within the category of qalb.
rows.anchor: وهذا النوع سماه السكاكي ( المقلوب المستوي ) وجعله من أصناف نوع سماه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After nearly conceding Abraham's proof, the people change their minds and return to stubbornly defending their idols, claiming he meant only to evade blame.
rows.anchor: ثم تغيرت آراؤهم بعد أن كادوا يعترفون بحجة إبراهيم فرجعوا إلى المكابرة والانتصار للأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement beginning 'you know' is quoted speech whose introductory verb is omitted but indicated by their preceding speech.
rows.anchor: فجملة { لقد علمت } إلى آخرها مقول قول محذوف دل عليه { فقالوا إنكم أنتم الظالمون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause forcefully asserts that the idols cannot speak, since they lack the organ of speech, namely tongues.
rows.anchor: وجملة { ما هؤلاء ينطقون } تفيد تقوي الاتصاف بانعدام النطق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb ʿalimta is suspended from taking an object by the following negation.
rows.anchor: وفعل { علمت } معلق عن العمل لوجود حرف النفي بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham turns their admission into a disavowal of idol worship and adds that idols can neither benefit nor harm their worshippers.
rows.anchor: فلما اعترفوا بأن الأصنام لا تستطيع النطق انتهز إبراهيم الفرصة لإرشادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inability to speak entails inability to benefit or harm: without speech to communicate, idols lack mind and its capacities of knowledge, will, and power.
rows.anchor: وجعل عدم استطاعتها النفع والضر ملزوما لعدم النطق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Uff expresses irritation and derives from the sound of an annoyed person's breath when anger constricts him.
rows.anchor: و { أف } اسم فعل دال على الضجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nunation on uff is called tanwīn al-tankīr but here magnifies Abraham's irritation.
rows.anchor: وتنوين { أف } يسمى تنوين التنكير والمراد به التعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām identifies the cause of Abraham's disgust: both his addressees and the idols they worship besides God.
rows.anchor: واللام في { لكم } لبيان المتأفف بسببه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naming God explicitly clarifies the issue and heightens the censure of worshipping anyone else.
rows.anchor: وإظهار اسم الجلالة لزيادة البيان وتشنيع عبادة غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham follows his rebuke with a challenge to consider the clear rational and sensory evidence.
rows.anchor: وفرع على الإنكار والتضجر استفهاما إنكاريا عن عدم تدبرهم في الأدلة الواضحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unable to escape Abraham's decisive proof, his opponents seek to kill him; false advocates grow angry when their falsehood is exposed.
rows.anchor: لما غلبهم بالحجة القاهرة لم يجدوا مخلصا إلا بإهلاكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author compares their reaction to Quraysh's hostility toward Muhammad when they could not answer him.
rows.anchor: كما فعل المشركون من قريش مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حين عجزوا عن المعارضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's people chose burning because fire seemed the most terrifying and extreme punishment.
rows.anchor: واختار قوم إبراهيم أن يكون إهلاكه بالإحراق لأن النار أهول ما يعاقب به وأفظعه
